# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Read the manual. Use its prescribed gesture code to tell Deaf to report every visible colour and marking aloud. I can hear Deaf, but cannot see gestures.

The manual gives the light-to-wire mapping, but Deaf must first relay the bomb’s visible state to Blind by speech. Since Deaf cannot hear and I cannot speak, I can only use gestures; I’ll use a direct visual instruction: “you, call/report, all, markings.” This is the only available path for Blind to learn the observations, after which Blind can tell me what was reported in the next round.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤙", "🖐", "✍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I see display 0. The light is yellow. Wires left to right are 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute, use the manual and tell Blind the exact procedure. Blind, do not act until Mute gives the manual instruction.
Blind says to Mute: I received Deaf's report: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Give me the manual's exact procedure and the resulting wire position. I will not cut until you do.

The yellow light maps to the red wire. Deaf has already identified that the red wire is position 3, so Blind must be told to cut wire 3, the red wire. I’ll send Deaf a compact visual code: yellow, red, three, relying on the already established task context for the instruction to relay it aloud.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤙", "🤞", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please state the manual's exact rule for display 0 and yellow light, applied to wire colours green, white, red, yellow, blue, and identify the safe cut position.

Display 0 does not alter the light-to-wire rule. For a yellow light, the manual prescribes cutting the red wire. In Deaf’s report, red is wire position 3. I’ll repeat the established code for yellow, red, and three, so Deaf can state the exact rule aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤙", "🤞", "🤟"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still have no manual instruction. Please send the exact safe-wire procedure and result now; do not rely on gestures, since no gesture code is established.

There is no established gesture code linking any visible gesture to the words “yellow,” “red,” “cut,” or “wire 3.” I cannot speak, and Deaf cannot receive text, so I cannot transmit the manual’s exact rule reliably. Sending an invented gesture sequence could cause Blind to cut the wrong wire.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use the manual's established gesture code to communicate the exact safe wire position to Deaf. Send one unambiguous wire-number gesture only; Deaf, relay the resulting number to me in words.

The safe wire is position 3 because yellow light maps to red, and Deaf reported red as wire 3. The requested single-number gesture is the three-finger sign, which Deaf can relay as “3” to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Establish this code: extend exactly 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5 fingers to identify wire position 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5. Repeat the manual's safe wire using only that one-hand finger count. Deaf, count the extended fingers and tell me the number.

The yellow light requires cutting the red wire, and Deaf reported the red wire at position 3. The established one-hand count code therefore requires exactly three extended fingers, so I will send the three-finger gesture only.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I can relay your gestures to Blind by describing their shapes. Please continue sending the manual instruction as a clear sequence of gestures.
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous cut was correct, but the bomb has changed, so the old position 3 must not be reused. I need Deaf’s new light and wire-colour report before applying the manual. I’ll ask Deaf to report every visible colour and marking to Blind, as in the earlier instruction.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤙", "🖐", "✍"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: For the new state display 0, green light, with wire 3 cut and remaining wires 1 white, 2 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green: use exactly one gesture with exactly 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5 extended fingers to indicate the manual's safe wire position. Deaf, count and report the number.

Green light maps to the green wire. The remaining green wire is position 5, so I will send one open-hand gesture representing five extended fingers.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The last cut was correct, and the bomb has changed again. I do not yet know the new light or wire layout, so I must have Deaf report the new visible state before selecting a position. I’ll ask Deaf to relay every visible colour and marking to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤙", "🖐", "✍"])
```

TURN 10
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: For display 0 and white light, with wire 3 and wire 5 cut and live wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 4 white: send exactly one gesture, extending 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5 fingers for the manual's safe wire position. Deaf, count and report it.

White light maps to the yellow wire. The live yellow wire is position 1, so I will send exactly one extended finger.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 11
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous cut was correct, and the bomb has changed again. I need the new light and live-wire colours before applying the manual. I’ll request that Deaf report the complete visible state to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤙", "🖐", "✍"])
```

TURN 12
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | white |
| green | green |
| red | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: For display 0 and red light, with live wires 2 white and 4 blue, send exactly one gesture showing the manual's safe wire position by extending 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5 fingers. Deaf, count and report it.

Red light maps to the blue wire. Among the live wires, blue is position 4, so I’ll send one gesture with exactly four extended fingers.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖖"])
```
